from docx import Document
from docx.shared import Pt, RGBColor, Inches
from docx.enum.text import WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH
from docx.enum.table import WD_TABLE_ALIGNMENT
from docx.oxml.ns import qn
from docx.oxml import OxmlElement

doc = Document()
sec = doc.sections[0]
sec.left_margin = sec.right_margin = Inches(1)
sec.top_margin = sec.bottom_margin = Inches(1)
st = doc.styles["Normal"]; st.font.name = "Calibri"; st.font.size = Pt(10.5)
for h,s in (("Heading 1",14),("Heading 2",12),("Heading 3",11)):
    doc.styles[h].font.name="Calibri"; doc.styles[h].font.size=Pt(s); doc.styles[h].font.color.rgb=RGBColor(0x1F,0x3A,0x5F)

def shade(cell, color):
    tcPr = cell._tc.get_or_add_tcPr()
    shd = OxmlElement("w:shd"); shd.set(qn("w:val"),"clear"); shd.set(qn("w:color"),"auto"); shd.set(qn("w:fill"),color)
    tcPr.append(shd)

def para(text, bold=False, italic=False, size=None, align=None, space_after=6):
    p = doc.add_paragraph()
    add_runs(p, text, bold, italic, size)
    p.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(space_after)
    if align: p.alignment = align
    return p

def add_runs(p, text, bold=False, italic=False, size=None):
    # support **bold** segments
    parts = text.split("**")
    for i, seg in enumerate(parts):
        if not seg: continue
        r = p.add_run(seg)
        r.bold = bold or (i % 2 == 1)
        r.italic = italic
        if size: r.font.size = Pt(size)

def bullet(text, level=0):
    p = doc.add_paragraph(style="List Bullet" if level==0 else "List Bullet 2")
    add_runs(p, text)
    p.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(3)
    return p

def numbered(text):
    p = doc.add_paragraph(style="List Number")
    add_runs(p, text); p.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(3)

def table(headers, rows, widths=None, header_color="1F3A5F", font=9, risk_col=None):
    t = doc.add_table(rows=1, cols=len(headers))
    t.style = "Table Grid"; t.alignment = WD_TABLE_ALIGNMENT.CENTER
    for i,h in enumerate(headers):
        c = t.rows[0].cells[i]; c.text = ""
        r = c.paragraphs[0].add_run(h); r.bold=True; r.font.size=Pt(font); r.font.color.rgb=RGBColor(0xFF,0xFF,0xFF)
        shade(c, header_color)
    for row in rows:
        cells = t.add_row().cells
        for i,v in enumerate(row):
            cells[i].text = ""
            add_runs(cells[i].paragraphs[0], str(v), size=font)
            if risk_col is not None and i == risk_col:
                col = {"Critical":"F4CCCC","High":"FCE5CD","Medium":"FFF2CC","Low":"D9EAD3"}.get(str(v).split()[0])
                if col: shade(cells[i], col)
    if widths:
        for row in t.rows:
            for i,w in enumerate(widths):
                row.cells[i].width = Inches(w)
    doc.add_paragraph().paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(2)
    return t

H1 = lambda s: doc.add_heading(s, level=1)
H2 = lambda s: doc.add_heading(s, level=2)
H3 = lambda s: doc.add_heading(s, level=3)

H1("III. Detailed Analysis")
para("Regulatory references are to the Illinois Insurance Code (215 ILCS 5/) and the Illinois Department of Insurance’s credit-for-reinsurance rules, which implement the NAIC Credit for Reinsurance Model Law (#785) and Model Regulation (#786). Before finalizing the markup we will confirm each requirement against the current Illinois text, including the Department’s current trust-agreement and reinsurance-agreement requirements and the status of Illinois’s reciprocal-jurisdiction provisions.", italic=True, size=9)

H2("A. Credit for Reinsurance and Collateral")
H3("A.1 Argonaut Re’s status drives everything")
para("Argonaut Re is not licensed, accredited or certified in any U.S. state (Trust Recitals and §9.01(f); B&R Summary §3.2). Pinnacle can therefore take credit only to the extent of qualifying collateral (trust, letter of credit or funds withheld) under 215 ILCS 5/173.1. B&R correctly notes that the standard for a non-certified unauthorized reinsurer is 100% of ceded liabilities: ceded UPR, ceded case and IBNR loss and LAE reserves, and balances due. Any shortfall becomes a provision for reinsurance that reduces surplus and RBC and could affect Pinnacle’s A.M. Best A- rating (B&R Summary §6). The stated purpose of the Trust Agreement (§2.02, §10.01; Treaty §18.2) is to obtain full credit. As drafted, it does not.")
H3("A.2 Trust amount is fixed and lags the liabilities")
bullet("The Minimum Trust Amount and the Required Trust Amount are both $43.0M (Trust §§1.08, 1.15; Treaty §18.3). Argonaut Re justified that figure as “approximately 75% of estimated ceded premium” in light of its BBB+ rating (Karides, Dec. 4). The rating is irrelevant to an uncertified reinsurer’s collateral requirement.")
bullet("Adjustment is annual, effective December 31, with 60 days to calculate (Trust §4.02). Any increase “shall be subject to the mutual written agreement” of Grantor and Beneficiary, and failing agreement the amount stays where it was (§4.02(b)). Argonaut Re can therefore block any increase, and in any event an increase lands after the year-end statement date it is meant to support.")
bullet("Trust §4.02 measures obligations by “ceded outstanding loss reserves and ceded loss adjustment expense reserves.” It does not expressly include ceded UPR or IBNR, even though Treaty §18.4 says the adjustment includes IBNR and UPR. The two documents must be conformed.")
bullet("Our illustrative model (Part IV) shows ceded liabilities peaking at around the December 31, 2025 annual statement date: about $47.0M in the base case and $52.5M at Lakeshore’s 95th percentile. The B&R Summary understates the exposure at that date. It says ceded UPR would be “zero (fully earned)” at December 31, 2025, but on a risks-attaching basis, policies written during 2025 remain roughly half unearned at year-end (about $28.95M of ceded UPR if writings are level).")
para("**Recommendation:** Required Trust Amount = the greater of (i) $43.0M and (ii) 102% (or at least 100%) of the Reinsurer’s Obligations, computed quarterly from Pinnacle’s statutory statements (including ceded UPR, case, IBNR, ALAE and amounts due). Argonaut Re must deposit any deficiency within 15 Business Days of notice from the Beneficiary, with no consent right. Reductions require Beneficiary consent. Alternatives Pinnacle could accept: an evergreen clean letter of credit from a qualified U.S. financial institution for the excess over $43M, or funds withheld on part of the ceded premium. Funds withheld would also address counterparty risk.")
H3("A.3 Grantor offset withdrawals (Trust Art. VII, Exhibit C)")
para("Trust §7.01 lets the Grantor, on delivery of its own Offset Notice, cause the Trustee to “adjust the Required Trust Amount” and withdraw assets equal to an offset claimed under any other agreement between the parties. Nothing requires Pinnacle’s consent, and the remaining balance need only meet the “adjusted” amount. That appears to override the $43M floor in §1.15 and §4.02(a). A credit-for-reinsurance trust must keep assets for the sole benefit of the beneficiary, and the grantor may withdraw only with the beneficiary’s written approval. Article VII is inconsistent with that model. It also exposes Pinnacle to self-help by a counterparty under stress. The cross-references to “Article VIII of the Reinsurance Agreement” (§1.10, §1.14, §7.01, Ex. C) are wrong: offset is Treaty Article XIII, and Article VIII is Profit Commission. **Delete Article VII and Exhibit C**, delete the offset qualifier in §1.14, and add an express covenant that trust assets are not subject to offset by the Grantor.")
para("Treaty Art. XIII is itself very broad. It is mutual, extends across all agreements past, present and future, can be exercised “at any time” without consent, and survives indefinitely (§13.2). If Pinnacle became insolvent, the receiver would apply 215 ILCS 5/206’s offset limitations, so the clause should state that it applies subject to that section. Commercially, Pinnacle should limit offset to balances under this Treaty, or at minimum exclude offset against trust assets and against amounts in dispute.")
H3("A.4 Conditions on Pinnacle’s withdrawal right (Trust §§5.01–5.02, Ex. A)")
para("§5.01 is good: withdrawal without notice to or consent of the Grantor, within two Business Days. §5.02 then limits withdrawals to five enumerated purposes “and for these purposes only,” requires the Beneficiary to certify the purpose, and builds in substantive conditions. Category (c) requires a balance unpaid for 30 days or more. Category (d) allows reserves to be funded only after termination, commutation or expiry. The credit-for-reinsurance model requires that the beneficiary be able to withdraw at any time on written notice to the trustee, with no other statement or document required. Restrictions on the use of withdrawn assets belong in the reinsurance agreement, together with the cedant’s obligation to hold any excess in trust or return it. **Recommendation:** in the Trust Agreement, provide only for unconditional withdrawal on written demand. Delete the purpose checkboxes and certification from Exhibit A, or reduce them to an acknowledgment. Add a conforming “permitted uses” covenant to Treaty Art. XVIII, which should also allow Pinnacle, on termination, on notice of non-renewal or on a trust deficiency, to withdraw the full amount of obligations into a separate account held for Argonaut Re.")
H3("A.5 Other trust mechanics")
bullet("**Substitution (§4.03):** the Grantor can substitute assets on five Business Days’ notice with no Beneficiary approval.
